title: Data centers become "killer application" for new power transformer tech
gist: AI data centers moving to DC power architectures have become the commercial wedge for solid-state transformers, which replace hand-wound 1880s-era copper-and-steel transformers with mass-manufacturable silicon carbide power electronics. Amperesand, Heron Power, and DG Matrix have raised over $280 million in a year, and NC State has demonstrated a 1 MW grid-connected unit — with the second-order payoff being relief of the multi-year transformer supply backlog choking all US grid expansion.

insights.claim: The largest power transformers cannot be mass-manufactured but are custom-built for each utility's substations, with two copper coils hand-wound around a steel core on a design dating to the 1880s.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Hand-assembly is the physical reason transformer supply cannot scale with demand — a hard constraint no amount of capital spending fixes quickly.
insights.quote: Power grids currently rely on conventional transformer technology that is painstakingly assembled by hand and has a fundamental design dating back to the 1880s.

insights.claim: Utilities and other customers must wait up to several years for delivery of new power transformers, which delays both grid expansion for growing electricity demand and the replacement of aging units.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Multi-year transformer lead times are the gating item on every US grid project — the binding constraint to watch in data center and renewables buildout timelines.

insights.claim: Relatively few specialized companies manufacture conventional transformers, whereas solid-state transformers are an electronics device, which an NC State professor argues completely opens up both who can compete and where transformers can be made.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: A shift from a concentrated oligopoly to a contract-electronics supply model would compress incumbent transformer makers' pricing power.
insights.quote: It completely opens up the space for who can play in the transformer space, and also opens up where transformers can be manufactured.

themes.theme: Why AI data centers are the wedge

insights.claim: Data centers have become the largest driver of surging US electricity demand and are straining power grids, but that same boom is accelerating investment in solid-state transformers.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The AI load problem is funding its own infrastructure solution — a rare case where the demand shock finances the supply fix.
insights.locator: Data centers have become the largest driver

insights.claim: Hyperscalers are adopting DC power architectures for racks packed with AI chips, and solid-state transformers convert grid AC directly into that DC without a separate AC/DC conversion device.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The DC rack architecture shift is what creates the technical requirement — vendors selling into legacy AC data centers do not have this pull.
insights.locator: Tech companies building the largest AI data centers

insights.claim: An NC State professor frames the solid-state transformer as a single box that eliminates a lot of infrastructure and gives one control location, removing interoperability conflicts where multiple data center components try to regulate the same thing.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Consolidating conversion stages is a capex and operational-complexity argument, which is what gets it past hyperscaler procurement rather than efficiency alone.
insights.quote: Now you have one conversion stage outside the data hall and then you just go straight to the rack.
insights.locator: It’s kind of this one magic box

insights.claim: Data centers are the killer application for solid-state transformers right now, and several US companies — Amperesand, Heron Power, and DG Matrix — have collectively raised more than $280 million over the past year to commercialize the technology.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Three named private companies with $280M+ of fresh capital define the investable universe in this category today.
insights.quote: killer application for solid-state transformers right now

insights.claim: Solid-state transformers could greatly reduce the copper and other materials needed by data center projects, while their smaller footprint frees up site space for other uses.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Material-intensity reduction is a modest bearish signal for copper demand from data center electrical buildout, and a land-efficiency argument for developers.

themes.theme: The technology and its demonstrated state

insights.claim: Solid-state transformers use high-frequency semiconductor switching for voltage conversion and can be mass-manufactured using semiconductor materials such as silicon carbide, making them smaller, lighter, modular, and capable of handling multiple tasks in one device.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Silicon carbide demand gets a new industrial end market beyond EV powertrains — relevant to SiC wafer and device supply chains.

insights.claim: NC State demonstrated a solid-state transformer connected to a live grid line handling up to 1 megawatt while charging an electric vehicle battery, performing both the voltage step-down and the AC-to-DC conversion in one unit.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: A live-grid 1 MW demonstration is the credibility milestone that moves this from lab curiosity toward utility procurement conversations.

insights.claim: The demonstration unit measures roughly 1 by 1.5 by 2 meters, has sat in a shipping container at EPRI's Lenox, Massachusetts power delivery lab since May 2026, and returns to NC State in September after months of summertime testing.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: This is still a single containerized prototype under environmental test — commercial deployment timelines should be measured in years, not quarters.

insights.claim: The crucial enabling component was a custom-made high-frequency isolation transformer able to sustain the full stress of the grid and full distribution voltage across a relatively compact device.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The bottleneck component is custom-built, not off-the-shelf — a key manufacturability risk to watch before mass-production claims are credible.
insights.quote: the “full stress of the grid, the full distribution voltage”
insights.locator: The solid-state transformer has a modular design

insights.claim: The NC State demonstration is the culmination of a collaboration with the New York Power Authority that began in 2018, indicating an eight-year development cycle to reach a single field prototype.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Grid hardware development cycles run near a decade — a sober counterweight to the funding momentum in this category.

insights.claim: Successful commercialization could ease the broader transformer supply chain shortage, making conventional transformers more available for grid upgrades and expansions unrelated to data centers.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The largest economic payoff is a spillover — every delayed grid project everywhere gets unblocked, not just the AI campuses that funded it.
insights.locator: In the long run, successful commercialization

insights.claim: The same DC-conversion advantage applies to EV charging, where a solid-state transformer replaces three blobs of steel with one and removes much of the wiring and trenching a charging site would normally require.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Installation labor and civil works — not the hardware — are where the EV charging cost savings land, which changes charger site economics.
insights.quote: It replaces three blobs of steel with one blob of steel and removes a lot of the wiring and trenching that you would typically have to do for an electric vehicle application.
insights.locator: It looks like a big transformer box

insights.claim: The professor's stated commercialization path is that data center adoption 'derisks' the technology for mass adoption elsewhere, with EV charging in dense areas and DC distribution inside homes as follow-on markets.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The classic high-margin-beachhead-to-mass-market path — watch for the first non-data-center order as the signal that derisking worked.
insights.quote: Beyond data centers, we can think about electric vehicle charging in densely populated areas
insights.locator: Engineering and commercialization challenges still lie ahead
